title: Partial-stream replay and structured-output fidelity adapter for OpenAI Chat compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an adapter layer that maps Redwood's streaming and function-calling runtime to OpenAI Chat Completions semantics while preserving structured-output fidelity and allowing partial-stream replay for client reconnects. This ticket focuses on the request/response shape transformations, incremental event checkpoints for resumed streams, and guarantees around function call emission order and idempotency metadata. Goal: allow legacy OpenAI-based clients to consume Redwood streams with minimal changes and avoid silent behavioural regressions during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter can translate Redwood streaming deltas to OpenAI-style chunked SSE frames and back-compatibly rehydrate them into full responses
Function calls emitted by the model are preserved in order and include a canonical idempotency token so clients can detect duplicates after reconnect
Partial-stream replay: a client reconnecting with a checkpoint token can resume from the last reliable event without duplicating tool invocations
Structured outputs (JSON blocks, tagged sections) pass a schema-enforcement hook; invalid or truncated fragments trigger a guarded fallback to a sanitized structured-output object
Automated tests for replay, fncall deduplication, and schema enforcement integrated into CI with coverage > 85% for adapter module
implementation_notes: Introduce 'replay_checkpoint' header emitted every N tokens (configurable; default 1024) containing stable event cursor and fncall cursor positions
Map Redwood streaming events -> OpenAI SSE lines using a deterministic framing serializer; include 'event_type' and 'cursor' fields in each line
Fncall preservation: attach a short sha1-based idempotency_token to every fncall event and surface it in both the SSE payload and standard response body for non-streaming fallbacks
Schema enforcement will run in a sandboxed transformer that can autocorrect common truncation artifacts (closing braces, incomplete arrays) and annotate corrections in telemetry
We will not change existing runtime kernel code; adapter lives in the conduit layer so it can be toggled per-customer via feature flag
risks: Adding checkpoints increases per-request metadata which may impact P50 latency if polling frequency is too high
Autocorrection of structured output could mask model regressions — must be surfaced in telemetry and allowed to be disabled per-route
Fncall idempotency requires downstream tool integration (customers must honor idempotency token) — partial guarantees otherwise
Replay state leakage: sensitive data must not be persisted in cursors; use HMACed cursors with short TTL
rollout_plan: Build adapter behind a feature flag and enable for 5 internal test clients
Run a canary with non-critical external customers (opt-in) for one week, monitor fncall duplication and structured-output correction counts
If metrics are OK, enable gradual ramp to 25% of hosted traffic, keep a kill-switch to revert mapping to passthrough
Document compatibility caveats and provide migration guide for customers to adopt native Redwood streaming semantics later
testing_plan: Unit tests for framing serializer and parser (edge cases: incomplete UTF-8, multibyte token splits)
Integration tests that simulate client disconnect and resume using replay_checkpoint tokens
E2E test with a toy tool that records idempotency tokens to ensure no duplicate tool effects after replay
Load test to measure latency and checkpoint overhead at 95th percentile under standard traffic profile
A small QA harness to fuzz structured-output payloads and validate autocorrection annotations
